chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn al-Arzymi, from his father, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When you wish to know that there is goodness in you, look at your heart. If it loves the people of obedience to Allah and hates the people of His disobedience, then there is goodness in you and Allah loves you. And if it hates the people of obedience to Allah and loves the people of His disobedience, then there is no goodness in you and Allah hates you. And the person is with the one whom he loves.

key_terms.الْمَرْءُ مَعَ مَنْ أَحَبَّ: The person is with the one whom he loves

ai.seo_question: How can I know if I have goodness in my heart according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This diagnostic criterion from al-Kafi emphasizes that spiritual health is determined by one's innate affinity for the righteous and aversion to the sinful, reflecting the Shia concept of *al-wala' wa al-barra*. The concluding phrase 'the person is with whom they love' links this internal state to the eschatological reality of resurrection, a theme deeply rooted in both Quranic and Hadith traditions.
